It also shows referral bonuses and a redemption control, making the reward-and-action solicitation part of the video's own promotion. the available video evidence does not establish that rewards were delivered or that every linked service operated as represented.

opening.argument: Judge the presentation as an explanation of what the app displays, not as a verified promise that every viewer will receive a gift card. The description explicitly says the video is for educational purposes, and the speaker says he will show a redemption-history screen. That combination supports a walkthrough reading. The record does not establish that the speaker guarantees delivery or asks viewers to pay for a reward.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies a free-gift-card title, an app link and ways to earn in the app. Those establish the subject and the demonstration, but not that a reward was falsely promised or withheld. Even its account acknowledges that the available evidence does not establish whether rewards were delivered. A task screen alone cannot settle that question.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The educational-purpose sentence does not undo the video's direct invitation to use the linked app. The title promises free Google Play gift cards, and the speaker tells viewers to follow the app link and describes bonuses, surveys, tasks and spins. Showing a redemption-history screen is part of that pitch; it does not establish that viewers receive the advertised rewards.

opening.argument: This is substantially a screen-by-screen gaming and app walkthrough. The video shows a YouTube comment picker reaching a named winner, then shows the rewards app's balance, redemption choices and Free Fire options. The speaker describes moving to redemption history. A judge can read those screens as demonstrations of interfaces and a giveaway process, without treating each displayed balance or redemption button as proof of an actual payout.

citations.quote: Now, I'm going to show you the proof of payment, so I go to Redim History. So I went to Redim History.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited task screen shows what the app offers; it does not by itself make the walkthrough a deceptive solicitation. The opening also omits the comment-picker sequence, which gives the video a concrete demonstration component beyond the app's earning tasks. The referral question is too unclear to establish any promised downline income.

citations.quote: So if you invite a friend and he invites a friend, how will you get it?

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A walkthrough can also be a promotion. Here the title foregrounds free gift cards, the description supplies an app link and referral code, and the speaker directs viewers to tap the app link. The comment-picker segment does not change what the app segment asks viewers to do, while the displayed balance and redemption options do not verify delivery.

opening.argument: The observable mechanism resembles an ordinary rewards promotion: the app displays discrete tasks with stated coin amounts, a wallet balance with referral bonuses, and a menu of redemption options. The description openly provides a referral code. Neither the cited screens nor the spoken invitation establishes a required deposit, a credential request or a guaranteed cash return. The referral activity is visible, but a visible referral bonus is not, on its own, evidence that participants must recruit others to obtain a reward.

citations.quote: Refer Code :- 2488 (Sivaji Gaming)

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats tasks and cascading referrals as suspicious, but the shown task list and transaction-history screen also fit a points-and-referrals service. The spoken referral line is a question, not a clear promise of income from successive recruits. No cited evidence establishes that a viewer must deposit money or surrender credentials to use the displayed redemption options.

citations.quote: So if you invite a friend and he invites a friend, how will you get it?

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a deposit or credential request does not resolve this case. The video attracts viewers with free Google Play gift cards, routes them to a coded app link, and describes bonuses, surveys, tasks and spins as earning activities. The displayed referral bonuses and redemption controls show how the promotion presents rewards, but do not establish that those rewards are delivered.
